hidden_pattern: The claim that unipolar PWM halves current ripple is false in general. For the single-leg unipolar scheme the exact ripple ratio is 2m/(1+m): 0.67 at m=0.5, 0.75 at m=0.6, and 0.95 at m=0.9, approaching 1 as the modulation index rises. Only the switching-loss proxy is exactly halved, because the single-leg scheme has two gate transitions per switching period instead of four. The dual-leg aligned scheme produces a two-pulse 0/+Vdc waveform: it halves the single-leg ripple (ratio m/(1+m), 0.375 at m=0.6) but switches both legs, so it doubles the loss proxy relative to the single-leg scheme. The naive phase-shifted dual-leg scheme is not even unipolar: it produces negative voltage pulses and a much larger ripple. 'Unipolar' names a family, not one waveform, and the quantitative claim depends on which member is chosen.
title: Unipolar against bipolar PWM: ripple depends on which unipolar
